# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III would take effect (medium confidence). Following the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) — formally adopted on 19 November 2025, politically agreed on 7 May 2026, and entering into force on 27 July 2026 — this deadline was officially postponed to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A small number of unconfirmed September 2026 reports claim a further delay to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU source and should be treated with significant caution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply, corresponding to 24 months after entry into force (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [EU AI Act August 2026 compliance](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance). This date was widely repeated across industry compliance guidance published prior to the Omnibus amendments [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20). One European Parliament summary instead describes a "36 months after entry into force" rule, which would imply a later date; this is likely a simplification inconsistent with other sources rather than a genuine alternative legal position (medium confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation on AI](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The AI Omnibus and Revised Timeline
The European Commission proposed the "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditioning the actual application date on confirmation that necessary harmonised standards and compliance tools would be available (medium confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The package went through a staged process: it was formally adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Digital Strategy - Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

Following this amendment, official EU Commission guidance confirms that Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). This is corroborated by multiple industry trackers [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I now apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence), a distinct, later timeline [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force).

The amended Article 113 is reported (low confidence) to specify that Chapter III Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027, though the source text is truncated and the full scope of exceptions is unclear [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). The consolidated EUR-Lex text dated 27 July 2026 reflects these post-Omnibus changes, including transitional provisions for systems already on the market (high confidence) [EUR-Lex 02024R1689-20260727](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727). Some sources attribute this change specifically to a new instrument, "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," though this citation is weakly corroborated (low confidence) [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html).

### Related but Distinct Deadlines
Annex III is a list of use-case categories that *may* trigger high-risk classification, not an automatic list of high-risk systems (low confidence) [Questa AI, "High-Risk Deadline Moved to 2027" (a)](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2). Separately, transparency obligations (Article 50) and certain prohibited practices (e.g., deepfakes, CSAM) follow independent timelines of 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively, and should not be confused with Annex III high-risk deadlines (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Three September 2026 news/blog sources claim a *second* delay, pushing the Annex III deadline to 2 August 2029 due to standards and notified-body readiness gaps (low confidence) [EU AI Act Legal Guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [AI Law Insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply), [Tech Legal Alerts](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline). This claim is **not corroborated by any official EU source** and directly conflicts with the Commission's own guidance stating 2 December 2027 [Digital Strategy - Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). Given the low confidence score and lack of an identifiable legal instrument, this claim should be treated as unverified or possibly erroneous.

## Knowledge Gaps
- No official source confirms or denies the alleged 2029 delay, nor cites a supporting legal instrument.
- The precise scope of Article 113 exceptions (beyond Article 6(5)) within Chapter III Sections 1–3 remains unclear.
- Whether harmonised standards and notified-body capacity issues—cited as justification for the 2027 delay—have since been resolved is unknown.
- The discrepancy between the "36 months" claim and the standard 24-month framing has not been reconciled.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III would take effect (medium confidence). Following the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline was officially postponed to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A small number of unconfirmed September 2026 reports claim a further delay to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU source and should be treated with significant caution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply, corresponding to 24 months after entry into force (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [EU AI Act August 2026 compliance](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance). This date was widely repeated across industry compliance guidance published prior to the Omnibus amendments [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20). One European Parliament summary instead describes a "36 months after entry into force" rule, which would imply a later date; this is likely a simplification inconsistent with other sources rather than a genuine alternative legal position (medium confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation on AI](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The AI Omnibus and Revised Timeline
The European Commission proposed the "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditioning the actual application date on confirmation that necessary harmonised standards and compliance tools would be available (medium confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). Political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and the package entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Digital Strategy - Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

Following this amendment, official EU Commission guidance confirms that Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force). This is corroborated by multiple industry trackers [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I now apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence), a distinct, later timeline [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force).

The amended Article 113 is reported (low confidence) to specify that Chapter III Sections 1–3 (excluding Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027, though the source text is truncated and the full scope of exceptions is unclear [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). The consolidated EUR-Lex text dated 27 July 2026 reflects these post-Omnibus changes, including transitional provisions for systems already on the market (high confidence) [EUR-Lex 02024R1689-20260727](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727). Some sources attribute this change specifically to a new instrument, "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," though this citation is weakly corroborated (low confidence) [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html).

### Related but Distinct Deadlines
Annex III is a list of use-case categories that *may* trigger high-risk classification, not an automatic list of high-risk systems (low confidence) [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2). Separately, transparency obligations (Article 50) and certain prohibited practices (e.g., deepfakes, CSAM) follow independent timelines of 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively, and should not be confused with Annex III high-risk deadlines (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Three September 2026 news/blog sources claim a *second* delay, pushing the Annex III deadline to 2 August 2029 due to standards and notified-body readiness gaps (low confidence) [EU AI Act Legal Guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [AI Law Insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply), [Tech Legal Alerts](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline). This claim is **not corroborated by any official EU source** and directly conflicts with the Commission's own guidance stating 2 December 2027 [Digital Strategy - Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). Given the low confidence score and lack of an identifiable legal instrument, this claim should be treated as unverified or possibly erroneous.

## Knowledge Gaps
- No official source confirms or denies the alleged 2029 delay, nor cites a supporting legal instrument.
- The precise scope of Article 113 exceptions (beyond Article 6(5)) within Chapter III Sections 1–3 remains unclear.
- Whether harmonised standards and notified-body capacity issues—cited as justification for the 2027 delay—have since been resolved is unknown.
- The discrepancy between the "36 months" claim and the standard 24-month framing has not been reconciled.
